The function $f$ is defined by the power series
$$
f(x)=-\frac{x}{2}+\frac{2 x^{2}}{3}-\frac{3 x^{3}}{4}+\cdots+\frac{(-1)^{n} n x^{n}}{n+1}+\cdots
$$

for all real numbers $x$ for which the series converges. The function $g$ is defined by the power series

$$
g(x)=1-\frac{x}{2!}+\frac{x^{2}}{4!}-\frac{x^{3}}{6!}+\cdots+\frac{(-1)^{n} x^{n}}{(2 n)!}+\cdots
$$

for all real numbers $x$ for which the series converges.\\
(a) Find the interval of convergence of the power series for $f$. Justify your answer.\\
(b) The graph of $y=f(x)-g(x)$ passes through the point $(0,-1)$. Find $y^{\prime}(0)$ and $y^{\prime \prime}(0)$. Determine whether $y$ has a relative minimum, a relative maximum, or neither at $x=0$. Give a reason for your answer.

\section*{Question 6}

The function \(f\) is defined by the power series
\[
f(x)=-\frac{x}{2}+\frac{2 x^{2}}{3}-\frac{3 x^{3}}{4}+\cdots+\frac{(-1)^{n} n x^{n}}{n+1}+\cdots
\]
for all real numbers \(x\) for which the series converges. The function \(g\) is defined by the power series
\[
g(x)=1-\frac{x}{2!}+\frac{x^{2}}{4!}-\frac{x^{3}}{6!}+\cdots+\frac{(-1)^{n} x^{n}}{(2 n)!}+\cdots
\]
for all real numbers \(x\) for which the series converges.
\begin{itemize}
\item[(a)] Find the interval of convergence of the power series for \(f\). Justify your answer.
\item[(b)] The graph of \(y=f(x)-g(x)\) passes through the point (0, -1). Find \(y^{\prime}(0)\) and \(y^{\prime \prime}(0)\). Determine whether \(y\) has a relative minimum, a relative maximum, or neither at \(x=0\). Give a reason for your answer.
\item[(a)] \(\left|\frac{(-1)^{n+1}(n+1) x^{n+1}}{n+2} \cdot \frac{n+1}{(-1)^{n} n x^{n}}\right|=\frac{(n+1)^{2}}{(n+2)(n)} \cdot|x|\)
\[
\lim _{n \rightarrow \infty} \frac{(n+1)^{2}}{(n+2)(n)} \cdot|x|=|x|
\]
The series converges when \(-1<x<1\).
When \(x=1\), the series is \(-\frac{1}{2}+\frac{2}{3}-\frac{3}{4}+\cdots\)
This series does not converge, because the limit of the individual terms is not zero.
When \(x=-1\), the series is \(\frac{1}{2}+\frac{2}{3}+\frac{3}{4}+\cdots\)
This series does not converge, because the limit of the individual terms is not zero.
Thus, the interval of convergence is \(-1<x<1\).
\item[(b)] \(f^{\prime}(x)=-\frac{1}{2}+\frac{4}{3} x-\frac{9}{4} x^{2}+\cdots\) and \(f^{\prime}(0)=-\frac{1}{2}\).
\[
g^{\prime}(x)=-\frac{1}{2!}+\frac{2}{4!} x-\frac{3}{6!} x^{2}+\cdots \text { and } g^{\prime}(0)=-\frac{1}{2} .
\]
\[
\begin{aligned}
& y^{\prime}(0)=f^{\prime}(0)-g^{\prime}(0)=0 \\
& f^{\prime \prime}(0)=\frac{4}{3} \text { and } g^{\prime \prime}(0)=\frac{2}{4!}=\frac{1}{12} .
\end{aligned}
\]
Thus, \(y^{\prime \prime}(0)=\frac{4}{3}-\frac{1}{12}>0\).
Since \(y^{\prime}(0)=0\) and \(y^{\prime \prime}(0)>0, y\) has a relative minimum at \(x=0\).
\end{itemize}
